cases.title: Supply-chain Control Tower
cases.sum: A management-reporting system for the whole supply chain: more than 10 source systems, over 100 KPIs and six business domains in one live view, on desktop and mobile.
sections: Challenge
The commercial division had no single tool for tracking the KPIs of its end-to-end process, from production to sales.

Operational data on output, shipments and sales sat in separate systems and reports, with no single source of truth. Several BI systems duplicated each other's data, and day-to-day operations ran on Excel reports compiled by hand at every stage of the supply chain. Analysing the current situation took too long, and decisions to deal with emerging risks came late.
Approach
Identified the key stakeholders and worked with cross-functional teams to define business requirements for the interface and functionality.
Selected the technology for data analysis and visualisation, assessing integration options for fast deployment, ease of use and flexible interface design.
Designed the configuration of a single reporting system and built a prototype dashboard with real-time KPIs for two production units.
Collected, verified and reconciled data from adjacent departments, and validated the consolidated data and collection methods.
Ran design control and functional testing, piloted and launched the system.
Wrote user guides and trained staff, then rolled the tool out to all departments.
ol
What we delivered
A data warehouse updated daily from more than 10 source systems.
Dashboards across six domains: commerce, logistics, production, economics, energy and ports.
Screens that can be tailored to an individual manager's requests.
A role model that gives different levels of access to the data.
A mobile version of the system.
Our role
hice coordinated the project and designed it end to end: visual design, UX/UI, testing and roll-out.
Outcome
Launched in August 2024, the system replaced manual reporting with one live view of the supply chain. Managers now monitor and analyse key metrics in one place:
live data on finished-goods warehouse loads at sites in every region;
the level of finished-goods sales across all business lines;
analysis of finished-goods stock held in warehouses.
Next steps
The roadmap moves the remaining indicators into a single KPI system with a profile for each executive, and adds scenario modelling, predictive analytics and AI assistants for working with data.

cases.title: Stocks in Ports
cases.sum: An analytical dashboard giving a complete, accurate picture of inventory held in ports for better planning and resource management.
sections: Challenge

Inventory held in ports was reported separately by each site, in different formats and on different schedules. Planners had no single, reliable picture of what was where, which made it hard to plan shipments and allocate resources.
Approach
Audited the data each port site produced and agreed one common structure for stock records.
Collected and consolidated data from every site and source into a single dataset.
Cleaned and standardised the records so figures from different ports could be compared directly.
Designed the dashboard around the questions planners ask every week: how much, where, and how it is changing.
ol
What we delivered
A consolidated stock dataset covering all port sites.
An analytical dashboard with an overview across ports and drill-down to each site.
A documented data blueprint showing how data moves from source to dashboard.
Outcome

Consolidated data improved the quality of analytics and sped up business-intelligence work. Logistics and supply-chain teams gained a shared view for strategic planning instead of reconciling site reports by hand.
quote: For the first time we see stock across every port in one place. Weekly planning that used to take two days of spreadsheet work now takes an hour.
Head of supply-chain planning, logistics company

cases.title: Fuel flows to power systems
cases.sum: Automated tracking and visualisation of how fuel moves to, and is consumed by, the company's power systems.
sections: Challenge

Data on how fuel moved to the company's power systems, and how it was consumed there, was collected manually and spread across several sources. Managers lacked a transparent, up-to-date view of fuel flows and the risks around them.
Approach
Mapped the fuel chain from delivery through storage to consumption by each power system.
Automated the collection and processing of fuel movement and consumption data.
Analysed the flows to show where fuel goes and how consumption changes over time.
Integrated the solution with the company's existing resource-management systems.
ol
What we delivered
An automated data pipeline for fuel movement and consumption.
Flow visualisations from source to each power system.
An implementation scheme showing how the solution connects to existing systems.
Outcome
Automation and visualisation gave transparency and control at every level, made the energy systems more efficient to manage, improved resource management and reduced operational risk.

cases.title: Packaging research for a consumer-device brand
cases.sum: A conference presentation of packaging research: goals, methodology, target audience and conclusions.
sections: Challenge

A consumer-device brand had completed research into its packaging and needed to present it at a conference. The audience had to follow the research quickly, from its goals to its conclusions, within a short talk.
Approach
Structured the talk as a research story: goals, method, audience, findings, conclusions.
Turned the research findings into charts and diagrams instead of text slides.
Designed the deck to be readable from the back of a conference hall.
ol
What we delivered
A conference presentation of the packaging research.
Visualisations of the research method, target audience and key findings.
Outcome
The brand presented its packaging research as a clear, visual story that the conference audience could follow from question to conclusion.

cases.title: Slide redesign for a microelectronics company
cases.sum: Redesign of corporate slides to reflect a modern company, follow the brand book and fit all master-deck content onto a single slide.
sections: Challenge

The company's existing slides no longer reflected a modern technology business. They had to follow the brand book, stay informative, and fit all of the information from the master version onto a single slide, for a deck emailed to partners and clients.
Approach
Reviewed the master slides and ranked the information by importance to partners and clients.
Rebuilt the layout on a grid from the brand book, so dense content stays readable.
Replaced text blocks with structured visuals where possible.
ol
What we delivered
Redesigned slides that keep all of the master-deck content.
A layout that works as a standalone email attachment, without a speaker.
The redesign
Two slides from the redesigned deck: a project overview and a company profile, each fitting a full master-deck section onto a single slide.

cases.title: Bank pilot: results for top management
cases.sum: Comprehensive analysis of a bank's pilot project, presented to the bank's top management.
sections: Challenge
A bank had run a pilot project since the start of the year and needed a comprehensive analysis of its results for top management: what worked, for which clients, and through which channels.
Approach
Processed the month-by-month analytical results since the start of the year.
Consolidated each month's data, grouped by client category and product type.
Identified the most effective client-acquisition channels within the pilot.
Visualised the data and surfaced the key insights.
Built the storyline and designed the presentation.
ol
What we delivered
A consolidated analytical dataset for the whole pilot period.
An executive presentation for top management with the key insights up front.
Outcome
Top management received a single, data-backed view of the pilot's results, with the most effective client-acquisition channels clearly identified.
quote: The team turned months of pilot data into a story the board understood in one meeting. The decision to scale was made on the strength of those slides.

cases.sum: An English-language company presentation promoting the bank and its products to an international audience.
sections: Challenge
OTP Bank needed an English-language presentation that would introduce the company, its history and its products to an international audience, and serve as a tool for promoting the bank abroad.
Approach
Organised the company's history and main achievements into a clear narrative for readers new to the bank.
Illustrated key products and services, highlighting their features and advantages over competitors.
Designed the deck to emphasise the bank's strengths and unique capabilities.
ol

An English-language company presentation.
Product and service slides that can be reused in partner and client meetings.
Outcome
The bank gained a presentation it can use to promote the company and its offer to international partners and clients.

cases.sum: A company presentation covering every one of AVED's business lines in detail.
sections: Challenge
AVED works across several business lines. The company needed one presentation that covers every area of activity in detail while staying easy to navigate.

Built an overview that shows how the business lines relate to each other.
Used visual navigation so readers can jump straight to the area they care about.

cases.title: Project 5-100: final results
cases.sum: Final results presentation for Project 5-100, the national programme to raise the global competitiveness of Russian universities.
sections: Challenge

Project 5-100 was the national programme to raise the global competitiveness of Russian universities. Its final results had to be presented clearly and fairly, including the fact that its ultimate goals were not reached.
Approach
Structured the results around the programme's original goals.
Showed what changed for participating universities, and where the goals were not met.
Turned programme indicators into charts that officials and university leaders can read the same way.
ol
What we delivered
A final results presentation for Project 5-100.
Charts and diagrams of the programme's key indicators.
Context

Project 5-100 was an important step in the development of Russian higher education, even though its ultimate goals were not reached. It raised universities' awareness of international standards and of the need to improve the quality of teaching and research.
quote: hice. took a decade of programme data and made the results clear to both officials and university leaders, without losing any of the nuance.

cases.title: Charts & infographics
cases.sum: A selection of charts and infographics: Sankey flows, chord diagrams, beeswarms, streamgraphs and editorial charts on energy, coal and trade.
sections: Challenge

Research teams in energy and commodities produce complex datasets: trade flows between countries, revenue distributions across industries, stock performance and energy mixes. Each finding needs a chart that makes its argument clear to readers of reports and articles.
Approach
Started from the finding, then chose the chart form that shows it best.
Used specialised forms where they fit the data: Sankey diagrams for flows, chord diagrams for two-way trade, beeswarms for distributions, streamgraphs for change over time.
Kept one visual system across all charts, so they read as a family inside reports.
ol
What we delivered
Export-flow Sankey diagrams.
Industry revenue distributions and clean-energy stock performance charts.
Country-level coal trade and energy-mix charts.
A full company infographic.
Outcome
A library of research and editorial graphics in a consistent visual language, ready to drop into reports, articles and presentations.
quote: Our analysts bring the numbers; hice. finds the one chart that makes the argument. Their graphics now carry our reports.

cases.title: Geo mapping
cases.sum: Relief maps, trade-flow maps and interactive choropleths – from coal power plants to China's net exports by province.
sections: Challenge

Energy and commodities research often depends on geography: where power plants are, how coal and other goods are traded between regions, how indicators differ by province. These stories need maps, not tables.
Approach
Used shaded-relief regional maps to place assets such as coal power plants in their landscape.
Built global trade-flow maps to show the direction and size of trade between countries.
Published interactive choropleths in Datawrapper, for example China's net exports by province, so readers can explore the data themselves.
ol
What we delivered
Shaded-relief regional maps.
Global trade-flow maps.
Interactive Datawrapper maps for online publication.
Outcome
Geographic data from the research became maps that work in print reports and as interactive graphics online.

cases.title: Sankey builder
cases.sum: A utility that aggregates data, builds Sankey diagrams and exports them automatically to vector and raster formats.
sections: Challenge
Sankey diagrams are a common way to show flows in research, but building them by hand from raw data is slow and error-prone, and every chart has to be exported in several formats.
Approach
Automated the aggregation of raw data into source-to-target flows.
Generated Sankey diagrams in our visual style directly from the aggregated data.
Added automatic export to vector and raster formats.
Built the utility with AI coding assistants.
ol
What we delivered
A utility that aggregates data and builds Sankey diagrams.
Automatic export to vector and raster formats.
Outcome
Sankey diagrams that used to be assembled by hand are now generated from data, with print and web formats exported in one step.

ol

VizForge, a data-visualisation tool with many chart types, styling options and export.

A full data-visualisation tool that turns a dataset into a styled, exportable chart in a few steps.
